findings.title: Validator performs a database write on every validation
findings.body: lib/validators/email_validator.rb line 13 calls BlockedEmail.should_block?(value) from inside validate_each, and should_block? increments match_count and saves the BlockedEmail record. Validation is supposed to be read-only but now does a write. UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save which validates again, so a single blocked signup increments match_count twice, and validations that fail for unrelated reasons or are run multiple times also inflate statistics and add extra writes to the signup path.

findings.title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive allowing bypass
findings.body: app/models/blocked_email.rb line 12 looks up BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first with the raw value and validates uniqueness case-sensitively with no downcasing on write. Email addresses differing only in case or surrounding whitespace will miss the block list, so an attacker blocked as bad@spammers.org can sign up as BAD@spammers.org or with different casing and the validator will not reject them.

findings.title: Non-atomic match_count increment loses updates
findings.body: app/models/blocked_email.rb lines 14-16 do record.match_count += 1 followed by record.save. Under concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked address this read-modify-write races and one increment overwrites the other, so match_count and last_match_at statistics become inaccurate. An atomic counter update such as increment_counter or update_counters should be used.

findings.title: change_email bypasses blocked/domain email checks
findings.body: app/controllers/users_controller.rb line 265 change_email only checks whether the address is already taken and then creates an email token, without running the User EmailValidator whitelist/blacklist or BlockedEmail check that signup runs. A user can therefore change their account email to a blocked or disallowed domain even though new signups with the same address are rejected.

findings.title: Wrong Ember dependent key prevents rejected email UI update
findings.body: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js line 96 declares emailValidation dependent on rejectedEmails.@each, but rejectedEmails is an array of plain strings. @each only observes properties on array items, so pushObject of a string does not invalidate the computed property. After a server rejection the email field will not immediately show as invalid until accountEmail itself changes. The dependent key should observe array membership such as rejectedEmails.[] or length.

findings.title: Moved whitelist/blacklist logic has no test coverage
findings.body: spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb only tests the new blocked-email branch. The whitelist/blacklist domain logic was moved verbatim from User#email_validator into EmailValidator but has no specs in this PR, so a regression in domain restriction behavior during the refactor would not be caught.
